title: Compromise of Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery Debts: Conditions of Acceptance
content:
### Clauses

1. *Retired clause, no longer in force:* the former opening clause that a debtor may offer a lump sum smaller than the balance to settle a debt. It is retired as a statement of when an offer may be made, and is not a basis for handling one.
2. An offer on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** is considered only with a Financial Status Report showing the debtor cannot pay the full amount within a reasonable time.
3. VA can accept a compromise only on a debt whose balance is not more than the debt type's compromise authority ceiling. A larger debt can be compromised only through the Department of Justice and is never decided on a service call. The balance is the one shown on the debt record.
4. An accepted amount must be paid in one lump sum within the debt type's lump-sum period, in calendar days of acceptance. When it is paid, the remaining balance is credited off and the debt closes as compromised; when it is not paid on time, the acceptance lapses and collection resumes.
5. Offers received within the collection-hold window hold collection like a waiver request.

### Authority test

| Balance on the debt record | Who can compromise |
|---|---|
| Not more than the ceiling (equal to it included) | VA |
| More than the ceiling | Only the Department of Justice; never decided on a service call |

### Hypothetical case

An offer of 3,000.00 USD on a debt of 8,000.00 USD, with a Financial Status Report, is accepted. If the 3,000.00 USD is paid in one lump sum within the lump-sum period, the remaining 5,000.00 USD is credited off and the debt closes as compromised. If it is not paid in time, the acceptance lapses and collection of the full balance resumes.

superseded_clauses: A debtor may offer a lump sum smaller than the balance to settle a debt.
